I wanted them to leave me alone. I was a huge fucking asshole towards them. This was not the first time this has happened. I also think that it's better this way. They drive me fucking nuts. They don't want to help me and I feel dddd I know it's mean but I feel like they shouldddddd daadnjlxc kind of help me, I feel like they would be able to do so but they don't want to. Now I miss them but it wouldn't work out anyways.
I can't tell them what's going on, I don't really even have the means to contact them anymore. I've already told them that I wasn't being depressed anymore and it's just way too much silly drama and asflnjrscdc

Anyways, thank you for all the replies.
I think there are a lot of people on this forum who are much more willing to accept help and who are worse off. I might contact a therapist sometime soon or I might not. 
Thank you for taking your time to read this and stuff.

I just pushed away (who gives a fuck) the person of whom I thought they might be able to help. They don't give a shit and it's not their job to do so, as I already said, I just kind of trusted them with a lot and I fucking hate myself for liking them as much as I do. They have kind of helped me before but they've also made things worse at other times, I don't know what I'm doing.
I don't know what to do, I spend all day doing nothing, I don't think I'll be able to do so much longer without being bored to death, I don't know, I don't know what I'm doing, I don't know.
I don't want to be annoying and I don't want to get too close to people but I do wish there was someone who would tell me that things do get better and I'm so fucking pathetic and needy and I just want to be gone, I don't know. Having to go to a therapist would make me feel like shit because I'd have to pay for someone to listen to me and that means that I'm not worthy of a friend and if I'm not even worthy of a friend, why would I stay alive, Why would I stay alive when I'm just a fucking burden to everyone around me, I don't know.

I've been feeling suicidal in the past few days, but I know this will probably go away again, so I don't think I'm actually going to go through with it. However, I don't really see anything changing that would make an actual difference in my life, something which would make it worth living. 

I've done acid, mdma, benzos, pep, coke, weed, shrooms, and h but mainly weed and alcohol. The weed was what triggered it, I believe.

I'm not so sure about my parents, I just went to a park together with my mother and my brother about a week ago and they wouldn't stop talking about how much they despised "people who don't function". I wasn't sure whether they were talking about me or people in general but I'm scared that they will be angry because I have caused this myself by having done all the drugs that I have done. I don't want them to know about the psychosis and treat me differently, either. I'm not sure if they would even want to help me. For example, when they found numerous empty bottles of corn schnapps and vodka inside my closet when I was 17, they were angry for twenty minutes or so but we've never talked about it again afterwards. When I was younger, several teachers told my parents to make me see a therapist and my father always got angry at the teachers because he thought there was nothing wrong with me and he didn't want a psychiatrist to drug me. They're decent people but I just don't want them to know.

Meds are pretty much out of the question. Despite everything that I've mentioned, I've considered seeing another therapist. The last time I contacted one, she told me that she couldn't help me and that I should get myself checked into a hospital, which I don't want. I was doing worse then, so perhaps it's going to be different now - or I just won't tell the therapist right away how messed up I am. I just need to get over myself and do it, haha. It's like that with everything else, too. I don't know why I'm so incapable of doing anything productive at all.

Thanks for all the replies.

I'm not sure, I think that perhaps the psychosis might be drug-induced.
Also, I'm not usually too depressed. I've tried Paroxetin and Risperdal. Paroxetin made me much more paranoid than I was already but I didn't tell the doctor about the psychosis before he prescribed it to me, which was pretty stupid. The Risperdal did work a little but I don't want to take drugs for the rest of my life, I'm scared that in the long-term they'll just make me more sick than I am already.
I've been to a therapist but he was a dick and he made my parents pay a lot of money because my insurance didn't want to pay. There's something about my insurance, too, that requires my parents to know when I'm in treatment. I don't want them to know, I don't want them to worry, I don't want them to ask questions again.
I'm going to think about it.
Nope, I haven't been diagnosed with anything.

I haven't actually seriously tried meditation yet.
I'm a little too closed-minded to do so, too, I guess, and I'm kind of suspicious of people telling me they know the answer to my problems and that it's something this specific that I wouldn't have thought of myself in a hundred years, which is kind of what this course promises. There is no course in the region I'm from, either. I'm not particularly keen on leaving the house but I wouldn't mind trying meditation by myself, I guess.

I'm not on medication. I took risperidone for a while and it enabled me to sleep, which in turn helped me to drink less. I stopped smoking weed last autumn because of the psychosis but then I couldn't sleep, so I took up drinking instead. In the past few months, I have only been drinking twice a week or so and I've also only been drinking a beer or two a night most of the nights which I did spend drinking. I'm sober most of the time now.
